fullPassage:
Save Coral Reefs

When you go deep into the sea, you can see a variety of marine animals including corals. Over the course of many years, corals build up to form large structures called coral reefs. Brightly colored coral reefs provide a beautiful underwater landscape. However, this is not the only reason they are valuable.

Importance of Coral Reefs

Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect both marine life and people living near the sea. Coral reefs provide shelter to an abundance of marine life, such as fish and underwater plants. Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs, they are often called "the rainforests of the sea." Nearly one quarter of all known marine species depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide themselves from predators, find food, reproduce, and raise their young in coral reefs.

As far as humans are concerned, over half a billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and survival. When large waves generated by storms rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the land on the shore from washing away and thus protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a source of medicine, and many organisms found in coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer. This is why they are sometimes referred to as the "medicine chests of the sea."

Coral Reefs in Danger

These underwater treasures are under threat of destruction. The more coral reefs become damaged, the more creatures relying on them will lose their homes. Thus, the increasing loss of coral reefs might lead to the destruction of the entire marine ecosystem. The U.N. reported that many of the world's coral reefs are currently endangered. In fact, nearly half of Australia's Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest, has disappeared. If swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.

What causes coral reefs to die? There are various causes, like destructive fishing techniques, overpopulation of corals' natural enemies, and careless tourism. However, the leading cause is the rise in water temperature due to global warming. The ideal temperature range for corals to live is 20°C to 28°C. When the water temperature rises above 30°C, coral reefs turn white and eventually die. Another serious cause is plastic waste. Plastic products, such as bottles and fishing lines, have been dumped into the sea. This spreads viruses and diseases, damaging coral reefs and their inhabitants.

Technologies to Save Coral Reefs

In recent years, advanced technologies have been put in place to save coral reefs by monitoring, protecting, and restoring them in quick and efficient ways. Researchers from Florida introduced a soft jellyfish-like robot to monitor coral reefs without damaging their delicate bodies. In addition, an Australian research team invented an intelligent underwater robot to protect coral reefs from a dangerous species of starfish. The robot uses a camera and computerized vision system to scan the reefs and identify this starfish. When it encounters one, the robot uses a foldable arm to inject some toxic salt into the starfish and eliminate it. Meanwhile, 3D printing systems have been proposed in Hong Kong as one way to restore coral reef structures. The 3D printer creates artificial support for corals. An example is a block made of mud that lies on the floor of the ocean. It is shaped in a way that allows corals to attach to it and grow easily.

Actions to Save Coral Reefs

Here are some simple but effective steps we can take in order to help protect coral reefs. First, you can avoid using beauty products containing tiny pieces of plastic because they pollute the oceans. Also, try not to use sunscreen made with certain chemicals that damage corals. Second, you can volunteer to help clean the beach. Recycling and reducing trash is a huge help in maintaining a clean ocean. Last but not least, make it known that coral reefs are in danger by spreading the word to people around you. Let people know about the threat to coral reefs and what actions to take to save them. This will make a big difference for the future.

questions.stem:

"The U.N. reported that many of the world's coral reefs are currently endangered."

det.korean: 유엔의 보고 → 'In fact(실제로)' 호주 사례로 구체화하는 흐름.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 앞의 '전체 해양 생태계 파괴'에서 유엔 보고 → 'In fact' 구체적 사례(호주)로 이어짐. ❌ ①: 첫 문장 바로 뒤는 비교급 구문과 맞지 않음. ❌ ②: 'Thus'가 앞의 인과관계를 받으므로 사이에 삽입 부적절. ❌ ④: 유엔 보고 후 구체 사례가 와야 하는데 ④ 뒤에 없음.
det.tip: 문장삽입: 'In fact'는 앞 문장의 구체적 예시를 도입. 유엔 보고 → In fact 호주 사례.

det.analysis: ✅ ①containing(포함하는): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ②pollute(오염시키다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ✅ ③damage(손상시키다): 원문 그대로, 적절. ❌ ④contaminating(오염시키다): 원문은 maintaining(유지하다). 바다를 '오염시키는 데' 도움이 된다는 건 반대 의미.
det.tip: maintaining(유지하다) ↔ contaminating(오염시키다). 깨끗한 바다를 '유지'하는 것이 맞다.

호주 연구팀은 해로운 불가사리로부터 산호초를 보호하는 로봇을 발명했다.
해파리 모양 로봇은 산호초를 복원하기 위해 만들어졌다.

det.korean: 호주 연구팀이 불가사리로부터 산호초를 보호하는 로봇을 발명했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'an Australian research team invented an intelligent underwater robot to protect coral reefs from a dangerous species of starfish.' 일치. ❌ ①: 플로리다는 모니터링용 해파리 로봇. ❌ ③: 3D 프린팅은 홍콩. ❌ ④: 해파리 로봇은 모니터링용.
det.tip: Florida = 모니터링 로봇, Australia = 보호(불가사리 제거) 로봇, Hong Kong = 3D 프린팅 복원.

questions.passage: What causes coral reefs to die? There are various causes, like destructive fishing techniques, overpopulation of corals' natural enemies, and careless tourism. However, the leading cause is the rise in water temperature due to global warming. The ideal temperature range for corals to live is 20°C to 28°C. When the water temperature rises above 30°C, coral reefs turn white and eventually die. Another serious cause is plastic waste. Plastic products, such as bottles and fishing lines, have been dumped into the sea. This spreads viruses and diseases, damaging coral reefs and their inhabitants.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 산호초가 죽는 원인에는 파괴적 어업, 천적 과잉 번식, 무분별한 관광이 있다.
수온이 28°C 이상이 되면 산호초가 하얗게 변하고 결국 죽는다.
플라스틱 제품은 바이러스와 질병을 퍼뜨려 산호초를 훼손한다.

det.korean: 수온이 30°C 이상이 되면 죽지, 28°C가 아니다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③: 원문은 'rises above 30°C'이므로 28°C가 아니라 30°C. ✅ ①: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②: 원문 그대로. ✅ ④: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: ideal range = 20~28°C (살 수 있는 온도). 30°C 이상 = 죽는 온도. 28°C와 30°C 구분 주의.

questions.passage: When large waves generated by storms rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they hit the coral reefs. __________, they prevent the land on the shore from washing away and thus protect towns near the sea. __________, reefs are a source of medicine, and many organisms found in coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 연결사로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 파도의 힘이 줄어든다. 결과적으로 해안을 보호한다. 게다가 약재 역할도 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Consequently — Moreover
❌ ② However — Therefore
❌ ③ Meanwhile — Nevertheless
❌ ④ Otherwise — Instead
✅ Consequently — Moreover: 첫째 빈칸은 인과(파도 감소 → 해안 보호), 둘째는 추가 정보. ❌ However — Therefore: 역접 후 인과, 맥락 불일치. ❌ Meanwhile — Nevertheless: 동시/양보, 맥락 불일치. ❌ Otherwise — Instead: 대안/대체, 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: Consequently(결과적으로): 원인→결과. Moreover(게다가): 추가 정보 나열.

questions.passage: Here are some simple but effective steps we can take in order to help protect coral reefs. First, you can avoid using beauty products containing tiny pieces of plastic because they pollute the oceans. Also, try not to use sunscreen made with certain chemicals that damage corals. Second, you can volunteer to help clean the beach. Recycling and reducing trash is a huge help in maintaining a clean ocean. Last but not least, make it known that coral reefs are in danger by spreading the word to people around you. Let people know about the threat to coral reefs and what actions to take to save them.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 산호초 보호를 위해 개인이 할 수 있는 실천 방법
산호초가 멸종 위기에 처한 과학적 원인
첨단 기술을 이용한 산호초 복원 방법

det.korean: 산호초 보호를 위한 개인적 실천 방법들(미세플라스틱 회피, 해변 청소, 인식 확산).
det.analysis: ✅ ①: 글 전체가 개인이 할 수 있는 구체적 행동(제품 선택, 봉사, 홍보)을 나열. ❌ ②: 원인은 이전 문단. ❌ ③: 경제적 가치 언급 없음. ❌ ④: 기술은 이전 문단.
det.tip: 'Actions to Save Coral Reefs' = 실천 방법. First, Second, Last but not least로 구조화.

questions.passage: (a) Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect both marine life and people living near the sea. (b) They provide shelter to an abundance of marine life. (c) Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs, they are often called "the volcanoes of the sea." (d) Nearly one quarter of all known marine species depend on coral reefs for survival.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 원문의 내용과 다른 부분이 포함된 문장은?

det.korean: (c)에서 '바다의 화산'이 아니라 '바다의 열대우림(rainforests)'이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (a)
❌ ② (b)
✅ ③ (c)
❌ ④ (d)
❌ (c): 원문은 'the rainforests of the sea'인데 'the volcanoes of the sea'로 변형. ✅ (a)(b)(d): 원문 그대로.
det.tip: rainforests(열대우림) ≠ volcanoes(화산). 원문의 핵심 비유 표현을 정확히 기억.

questions.stem: 다음 우리말을 주어진 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오. "신속한 조치가 취해지지 않으면, 과학자들은 대부분의 산호초가 2050년까지 파괴될 것으로 추정한다." [조건] if / swift action / estimate / destroy 를 포함하여 쓸 것 (17단어)
questions.wa: If swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.
accept: IF SWIFT ACTION IS NOT TAKEN, SCIENTISTS ESTIMATE THAT MOST CORAL REEFS WILL BE DESTROYED BY 2050.
If swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050
If swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.
if swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.
if swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050

det.korean: 신속한 조치가 취해지지 않으면, 과학자들은 대부분의 산호초가 2050년까지 파괴될 것으로 추정한다.
det.analysis: If swift action is not taken(수동태 조건절) + scientists estimate that(주절) + most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050(명사절, 수동태).
det.tip: 핵심 구조: if절(수동태) + estimate + that절(미래 수동태). 수동태 2번: is not taken, will be destroyed.

questions.ans: If swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.
